description: Index of all benchmark result sets for the GPU-SSM mismatch study
hypothesis: GPUs don't convert SSM arithmetic savings into proportional speed/energy gains because they're physically built for dense matmul, not sequential recurrence

result_sets.key_findings: SSM 100-200x slower than attention, <0.2% bandwidth utilization
SSM gap widens on A100 — 1000-1500x slower, <0.1% bandwidth utilization

conclusion: Not concluded. These runs compare naive reference implementations on both sides (Python for-loop SSM vs plain matmul attention, batch size 1), so the measured gap is dominated by kernel launch overhead and does not test the hypothesis. The go/no-go decision is pending strong baselines: FlashAttention-2, official Mamba CUDA kernels, a fused Mamba block, CUDA graph capture, and pynvml energy telemetry. Downstream design work in the Kalman project is blocked on that decision. Corrected 2026-10-13; measured values in the result sets are unchanged.
